messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: enable_if_c and disable_if_c
parts:
Daniel and I just found a new metaprogramming toy, the enable_if_c
and disable_if_c functionality in Boost.

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/utility/enable_if.html

It should make the refactoring we're about to undertake a lot easier,
because we can more explicitly control template instantiation.

Boost's implementation exploits the substitution-failure-is-not-an-error
(SFINAE) idiom. Using it is much simpler; here's how it works on
functions (wrapping the return type -- if the first template argument
to enable_if_c evaluates to true, the template's enable and otherwise
it's not. There are also ways to use this in class templates.

--------------------------------------
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <boost/utility/enable_if.hpp>
#include <boost/type_traits/is_arithmetic.hpp>

template <typename T>
typename boost::enable_if_c<boost::is_arithmetic<T>::value, T>::type
foo(T x) {
return x + 1;
}

template <typename T>
typename boost::disable_if_c<boost::is_arithmetic<T>::value, T>::type
foo(T x) {
return x;
}


int main() {
std::cout << "foo(1)=" << foo(1) << std::endl;
std::string bar("bar");
std::cout << "foo(\"bar\")=" << foo(bar) << std::endl;
}
----------------------------------

- Bob

This sounds good. I wonder if it can be used in combination with Eigen 3.2 (in beta now), whose primary new feature seems to be a Reference to an expression

http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox-devel/classEigen_1_1Ref.html

These are intended to reduce temporaries, but it seems like we could also enable_if / disable_if depending on whether T is an Eigen thing.

Ben

P.S. With the Eigen 3.2 beta, almost everything in test-unit fails because it can't compile agrad/matrix.hpp because it can't find an appropriate log function.
